title: Interprofessional Operating Room Debriefing
summary: In aviation, it is standard practice to hold a debriefing with all personnel involved in the flight after landing, and this is an important part of flight safety. However, such debriefings are not currently carried out after surgical procedures, even though they are a comparable situation with similarly high safety requirements. In addition to safety aspects, a debriefing could also increase employee satisfaction at various levels. Therefore, a structured debriefing should be conducted after the end of an operation. Questionnaires are used to assess the situation before the debriefing is introduced. After certain intervals following the introduction of the debriefing, the questionnaires are repeated to measure the improvement.

interventions.name: The individuals from different professional groups involved in an operation undergo a structured interprofessional debriefing (IORD) after each operation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Native speaker level German
Employment or comparable position at the University Medical Center Schleswig-Holstein
Participation in surgery within the scope of one's own profession
Exclusion criteria:
Age under 18
